channel.title: Journalism Quality Filter — Weekly Top 3
channel.description: The top three podcast episodes of the week (best from each feed), selected by AI for journalism and news quality. Updated weekly on Fridays.

item.title: Amanda Carpenter and Evan Gershkovich: Trump's and Putin's Authoritarian Projects
item.description:
Vigilance is still in order, but Trump’s efforts to rig the midterms have so far flopped. And that includes Trump’s self-sabotaging of his own plan to blame China for hacking our voting machines. But should the Dems win back Congress, they’re going to be busy tracing all the money that was stolen for the ballroom, the arch, and Pentagon contracts with Trump family members. Plus: Evan discusses his new book, which memorializes both his 16 months in Russian captivity—and the recent history of Russia at war under Putin.

Amanda Carpenter and Evan Gershkovich join Tim Miller.

show notes:

  • Evan’s book, “This Cursed Beautiful Land”
  • Protect Democracy’s Substack
  • Andrew in “Morning Shots” on impeaching Trump again
  • Sam and Will on Texas’s Bo French
  • The Bulwark’s campaign to help the Haitian community of Springfield
  • The Bulwark store
[Journalism Quality Filter — Quality: 8/10 — Features a substantive interview with Evan Gershkovich and focuses on authoritarian abuses and accountability with primary-source perspective.]

item.title: Bill Gates’s Blunt Warning on A.I.
item.description:
Bill Gates thinks A.I. alarmism hasn’t gone far enough. He believes the years ahead will be marred by catastrophic cyberattacks, bio-terrorism and mass job loss unless the government acts, because he thinks the idea that the A.I. industry can just self-regulate is “insane.”
I was struck in the conversation by how genuinely afraid Gates seemed to be that we are not ready for the consequences of what we are building, and how emphatic he was that so many of the people in positions of authority are in complete denial about what he thinks is about to happen.
Gates is a pioneering technologist, the co-founder of Microsoft and the chair of Gates Foundation, which is set to spend down around $200 billion over the next two decades. He recently announced that trying to make A.I. a force for equality in the world, as opposed to an impetus for inequality, is a new priority of his foundation’s work.
[Journalism Quality Filter — Quality: 8/10 — Presents a significant, clear interview with Bill Gates as a primary source on AI risks and governance, adding expert insight.]

item.title: DHS Called It False. Then It Was Confirmed.
item.description:
Daily Wire immigration reporter and Dao Prize nominee Jennie Taer joins Tim Rice to go behind her explosive exclusive: ICE officers across the country say they were verbally ordered to stop arresting illegal immigrants without criminal records. The order closely echoed Biden-era policy, the opposite of the mass deportation agenda many Trump voters were expecting. Within hours, DHS called the report false. Then Fox News and CBS helped confirm it, new verbal orders reversed course, and Vice President JD Vance acknowledged a communication breakdown. Jennie explains why frustrated officers came to her, who might have been behind the order, why something this big was never put in writing, and what it's like to break a story the federal government says isn't true. item.title: ‘This Is Nuts.’ An OpenAI Insider Explains Why He Quit.
item.description:
Last week, David Robinson resigned from OpenAI. He’d been in charge of writing the safety reports for new models and came to believe that OpenAI and the broader artificial intelligence industry lack the safety culture necessary to protect the world from what they’re building.
Robinson has an unusual background for an A.I. frontier lab staffer. He’s a Rhodes scholar and Yale Law graduate, he founded a civil rights nonprofit and he advised the Biden White House. He did not come up in the hothouse of Silicon Valley. And when he joined OpenAI in 2023, he says, he saw A.I. as a useful tool, not as a technology that could pose catastrophic risks.
That’s changed. In Robinson’s first interview since leaving OpenAI, he tells me why.
(The New York Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft claiming copyright infringement. The companies have denied those claims.)
[Journalism Quality Filter — Quality: 8/10 — A primary-source interview with a former OpenAI insider delivers original, first-hand accountability testimony on AI safety culture.]

item.title: America 250: History vs. Mythology with Annette Gordon-Reed and David Blight
item.description:
As America prepares to celebrate its 250th anniversary, Jon is joined by Yale historian David Blight and Harvard historian Annette Gordon-Reed to examine the battle being waged over our national story. Together, they explore why origin stories matter to nations and individuals, discuss how a fuller understanding of American history challenges national myths, and consider how we can continue to aspire toward our founding ideals even as we reckon with our failures. Plus, Jon answers listener questions on Trump at 250, the Knicks, and Taco Bell, hopefully for the last time.
